title: Funnel mapper and telemetry safety net for usage events
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a resilient funnel-mapper service that normalizes and maps disparate usage events from Console (UI, SDKs, webhooks) into a stable canonical envelope, applies progressive schema validation, and provides a safe fallback path when an event fails strict validation. Goal is to reduce event loss and downstream breakage for dashboards, billing, and alerting while enabling schema evolution without customer-facing regressions. Scope includes ingress transformation service, lightweight validation ruleset engine, provenance metadata, sampling policy for malformed events, and admin controls in Console to inspect and replay quarantined payloads.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: aligned with PM/Analytics on scope. Decided to start with console/web and SDK events first, postpone 3rd-party webhook normalization to follow-up.

2026-03-04 — Spike results: prototype mapper using JSON Schema + custom coercion had 92% match on historical 30-day sample. Performance baseline: median add latency ~4ms per event in Go microservice with worker pool; acceptable for current pipeline.

2026-03-06 — Design review notes from PM (E. Ramos): prefer progressive enforcement by route: ingest -> soft-validate -> hard-enforce on billing events. Action: add route-level policy config and admin override.
2026-03-07 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/compare/PR-1424 implementing envelope + provenance fields. Link in attachments.
2026-03-08 — Risk: potential spike in quarantined events after deploy. Mitigation: add sampling + auto-retry + dashboarding for quarantined counts. Dan to own alert thresholds.
2026-03-09 — Infra note: need an additional small Redis instance for short-lived mapping cache; ops should approve capacity change.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming console/web and SDK events are mapped into canonical envelope with stable set of required fields (event_type, timestamp_ms, user_id, tenant_id, route) for >=99% of 30-day sample.
Soft validation path: malformed or missing non-critical fields are coerced or stamped and forwarded to downstream with provenance.metadata.tag="soft-valid".
Hard enforcement path for billing and compliance routes rejects events missing required billing keys, writes to quarantine store, and emits alert when rate exceeds threshold.
Quarantine UI: console operators can list, inspect, annotate, and trigger replay for quarantined events via Console -> Telemetry -> Quarantine.
End-to-end latency impact on p95 for the ingestion pipeline remains within +10ms vs baseline for steady traffic at current fleet sizes.
Automated unit + integration tests covering schema transformations and fallback behaviors are added and included in CI.
Monitoring: dashboards created for mapped / soft-valid / quarantined / replayed counts and taxonomy, with alerting rules documented in runbook.
steps: Implement canonical envelope definition and publish as Confluence spec (initial draft).
Build lightweight mapper service in Go with plugin points for per-route transformations and a small LRU cache for common mapping rules.
Integrate JSON Schema validator + custom coercion hooks; expose route-level policy flags (soft vs hard).
Create quarantine store (S3 partitioned) and lightweight index in DynamoDB for fast listing and replays.
Add admin endpoints and UI hooks for Console Quarantine view; wire RBAC checks for access.
Add dashboards (Grafana) and alert rules; update telemetry runbook with incident playbook.
Load test with replayed 30-day traffic sample and measure p50/p95/p99 latency and quarantine rates.
decisions: Use a canonical envelope approach rather than trying to support multiple evolving schemas in downstream services — simplifies downstream contracts.
Progressive validation chosen: default=soft-validate for non-billing routes; explicit hard validation flag for billing/compliance routes.
Quarantine store implemented as S3 + DynamoDB index to keep operational complexity low and enable long-term retention for audits.
Language/runtime: Go for mapper service for low latency and existing infra familiarity; small Node adapter for quick dev debug UI integration.
Do not block deployment on 3rd-party webhook normalization; treat as separate incremental epic.
notes: Historical incident: 2025-11 dashboard outage caused by sudden schema change from SDK v2.5 — we aim to prevent similar hard failures by using soft-validation and replay workflow.
Estimated infra cost: small S3 + DynamoDB + one extra redis node; ops estimate ~ $120/month incremental during pilot.
We should coordinate with Billing team two weeks before enabling hard enforcement on billing routes to ensure SDK customers are prepared.
Follow-up work: SDK version tagging in envelope and migration tooling for gradual rollout (separate tickets).
